name: Learn basic boxing footwork
blurb: Footwork is the foundation everything else sits on. Stance, step-and-drag, pivots and angles are all learnable in a mirror without a partner or a bag.
gear: Optional: floor tape to mark a line
steps: Build the stance: feet shoulder-width and staggered, weight balanced, knees soft, hands up, chin tucked, elbows in.
Learn the step-and-drag: the lead foot moves first when going forward, the rear foot first when going back. Feet never cross.
Practise moving in all four directions while maintaining the stance — three-minute rounds on a taped line.
Learn the pivot off the lead foot to change angle without losing balance.
Add the slip and roll while moving, so head movement and feet work together.
Shadow-box three rounds focusing purely on feet, no punches at all.
tips: Crossing your feet is how people get knocked down. If they cross, slow down.
Stay on the balls of your feet without bouncing — flat heels make you slow, bouncing makes you tired.
proof: Three unbroken rounds of movement in all directions with your stance intact throughout.
